resolution.resolved_phrase: [Asym] is generated through exclusion of inadmissible observation orientations under a boundary interaction; symmetry itself remains the underlying relational whole.

layer_separation.symmetry_whole: >S< remains present and is never an exclusion target.
layer_separation.orientation_filter: Excl_obs_x removes or marks orientations inadmissible relative to B_x and D_rel.
layer_separation.admissible_family: Omega_x_adm is the remaining admissible orientation family.
layer_separation.dominant_orientation: o_x is a selected representative or equivalence class from Omega_x_adm; uniqueness is not assumed.

selection_rule.requirement: DomOrient_x must declare whether dominance means selection, ranking, quotient representative, or equivalence-class formation.
selection_rule.uniqueness: OPEN; multiple admissible orientations remain possible until a selection or quotient rule is supplied.
selection_rule.failure: If Omega_x_adm is empty, no bounded distinguishable expression is realized under the declared interaction and domain; this does not imply symmetry absence.

semantic_guards: Symmetry is not excluded, destroyed, negated, or removed.
Exclusion targets observation orientations or orientation relations only.
[Asym] is a symmetry condition, not the opposite of symmetry.
Dominant orientation does not imply a unique orientation without an explicit rule.
An empty admissible orientation family is a bounded-realization failure, not ontological nothingness.
canonicalization_action_required: Human review may qualify the legacy textbook wording using the resolved phrase; no automatic textbook or registry edit is authorized by this note.
falsification_conditions: A valid construction requires excluding the symmetry whole rather than observation orientations.
Dominance cannot be defined without presupposing the completed bounded identity.
The same admissible orientation family yields incompatible dominant orientations without a declared equivalence or ranking rule.
